turnpike.title: Lancaster County wheat
turnpike.lead: Some of the richest farmland in America
facts: Farms around Lancaster grow wheat and grind it into flour
The buyers are in Philadelphia, 60+ miles away
Every barrel has to go by wagon

turnpike.title: Stuck in the mud
turnpike.lead: Dirt roads turn to soup in spring rain and thaw
facts: Loaded wagons sink to the axles
Hauling a ton 30 miles by wagon can cost as much as shipping it across the Atlantic
Slow roads mean spoiled goods and lost days

turnpike.title: 62 miles of stone road
turnpike.lead: Philadelphia to Lancaster, with a stone bridge over the Brandywine
facts: The first long-distance paved road in America
Nine toll gates along the route
Open in every season

turnpike.title: Built in layers
turnpike.lead: The way they build roads in Europe
facts: Big broken stone at the bottom, gravel on top
Higher in the middle so rain runs off
Ditches on each side carry the water away

turnpike.title: Pay at the pike
turnpike.lead: A spiked pole, the "pike," blocks the road until you pay
facts: Pay the toll and the pike is turned aside: a "turnpike"
Tolls are charged per wagon, rider and horse
The money goes to the shareholders

turnpike.title: 1,000 shares at $300
facts: Shareholders own the road together
Profits from tolls are paid out as dividends
The law caps dividends at 15% a year

turnpike.title: Shares by lottery
turnpike.lead: So many people signed up that names were drawn from a wheel
facts: More buyers than shares
If money runs short, the company sells more shares
More shares means a smaller slice for each owner

turnpike.title: Pays year after year
turnpike.lead: Every wagon, every trip, every season
facts: Income depends on how much traffic uses the road
Slow and steady, not fast and big
"It won't make you rich by Christmas"

slater.title: Thread made by hand
slater.lead: In America, yarn is still spun one strand at a time
facts: Families spin at home on a spinning wheel
Weavers buy most of their fine thread from England
England's machines spin dozens of threads at once

slater.title: England's secret
slater.lead: British law guards the textile machines
facts: Exporting the machines or their plans is forbidden
Skilled mill workers are not allowed to emigrate
England wants to be the world's only cotton-thread factory

slater.title: The plans: memorized
slater.lead: Samuel Slater, age 21, carried nothing on paper
facts: Apprenticed for years in Jedediah Strutt's English mill
Strutt was partner to Richard Arkwright, inventor of the water frame
Every gear, roller and spindle, kept in his head

slater.title: Across the Atlantic
slater.lead: England to New York in 1789, then on to Rhode Island
facts: Traveled as a farm worker, not a mechanic
Wrote to Moses Brown, a Providence merchant, offering his skills
Brown's firm, Almy and Brown, hired him

slater.title: 72 spindles running
facts: Carding machine: combs raw cotton into a soft rope
Spinning frame: stretches and twists it into yarn
72 threads spun at the same time

slater.title: Water power
slater.lead: The falls of the Blackstone River at Pawtucket
facts: Falling water turns the wheel
Shafts, gears and belts carry the power to every machine
No horses, no fuel to buy

slater.title: One mill, many spinners
slater.lead: The promise: the work of hundreds of hand spinners
facts: Machine yarn is even and strong
Sold to weavers who make cloth at home
Every skein sold is one England doesn't sell

slater.title: The workers: children
facts: The first workers were children, some as young as 7
They piece broken threads and tend the frames
Long days, six days a week

slater.title: The only one in America
facts: No other working mill of this kind in the country
The whole secret is in one man's head
Being first means finding customers first

steamboat.title: The boat that needs no wind
steamboat.lead: Built by Robert Fulton, backed by Robert Livingston
facts: No sails, no oars, no mules
Critics called it "Fulton's Folly"
Its steam engine was built in England

steamboat.title: 150 miles up the Hudson
steamboat.lead: New York City to Albany, August 1807
facts: About 5 miles an hour, against the current
About 32 hours to Albany
A sailing sloop can take days, if the wind cooperates

steamboat.title: Fire, steam, paddles
facts: A wood fire boils water in the boiler
Steam pushes a piston back and forth
The piston turns the paddle wheels

steamboat.title: Runs on a schedule
steamboat.lead: Leave on time, arrive on time
facts: Sloops wait for the wind; steam doesn't
Passengers, freight and mail
Merchants will pay extra to know when goods arrive

steamboat.title: Exclusive rights
steamboat.lead: Granted by the New York legislature
facts: Only Livingston and Fulton may run steamboats in New York waters
Every river and lake in the state
Extended for 30 more years

steamboat.title: Rivals seized
steamboat.lead: Unlicensed steamboats can be taken by the state
facts: Competitors need Livingston and Fulton's permission
No price war, no rival schedules
The whole business rests on this law

steamboat.title: Buy the whole river
steamboat.lead: A share of every fare on the Hudson
facts: Fares from passengers
Fees for freight and mail
More boats planned for more routes

steamboat.title: Returns: enormous
facts: A second boat is already on order
Exact figures: not shown
"Shares like this don't last"

erie.title: The gap
erie.lead: The Hudson River in the east, Lake Erie in the west
facts: The Hudson carries goods from Albany to New York City and the sea
363 miles of forest, hills and swamp to Lake Erie
No river connects them

erie.title: A continent of farms
erie.lead: Beyond Lake Erie: wheat, timber and new settlements
facts: Settlers are pouring into Ohio and the Great Lakes country
Their crops have no cheap way to eastern markets
Much of that trade floats down to New Orleans instead

erie.title: $100 a ton
erie.lead: What a wagon charges to haul goods from Buffalo to New York City
facts: Weeks on muddy roads
Heavy goods cost the most to move
Too expensive for heavy, cheap goods like grain

erie.title: A canal from Albany to Buffalo
facts: 40 feet wide, 4 feet deep
Mules walk a towpath and pull the boats
One mule team can pull a 30-ton boat

erie.title: 83 locks
erie.lead: Stone chambers that lift boats uphill with water
facts: The boat enters and the gates close
Water flows in and the boat rises
568 feet of rise from the Hudson to Lake Erie

erie.title: $100 becomes $10
erie.lead: The promise: freight at a tenth of the price
facts: Wagon: about $100 a ton
Canal: about $10 a ton
Cheap freight means western grain can sell in the East

erie.lead: Estimated cost, built by the State of New York
facts: The biggest project ever tried in America
Ground breaks July 4, 1817, at Rome, New York
Backed by Governor DeWitt Clinton

erie.title: The Canal Fund
facts: Every boat pays a toll
Taxes on salt from Onondaga go in too
The fund pays interest, then repays the loan

erie.title: "Clinton's Folly"
erie.lead: Critics call it a ditch to nowhere
facts: Congress and President Madison refused federal money
No American has built anything like it
New York will build it alone

erie.title: And winter?
erie.lead: "Only a brief rest for the mules"
facts: Canal water freezes in the cold months
Boats wait for the spring thaw
Farm harvests come in late summer and fall

northerncross.title: Illinois is booming
northerncross.lead: The newest boom state in the West
facts: Settlers are pouring in from the East and the South
Chicago just became a city
The state capital is moving to Springfield

northerncross.title: Done with rivers
northerncross.lead: Rivers freeze in December and run low in August
facts: Riverboats stop when the water does
Wagons sink in prairie mud
A railroad runs on its own track

northerncross.title: 1,300 miles of railroad
facts: About $10 million for railroads, rivers and a canal
Paid for by selling State of Illinois bonds
Lines planned to cross the whole state

northerncross.title: The Northern Cross
northerncross.lead: Quincy to Springfield to the Indiana line
facts: From the Mississippi River across the state
Through the new capital at Springfield
The first line to be built

northerncross.title: Locomotive ordered
facts: A steam engine on wheels
Pulls a line of cars on rails
Baltimore began building America's first railroad in 1828

northerncross.title: 3 trains a week
facts: Passengers, crops and mail
Faster than any wagon or riverboat
Backed by the State of Illinois

northerncross.title: Strap rail: half the price
northerncross.lead: A wooden rail with a thin iron strap on top
facts: Solid iron rails must be shipped from England
Oak for rails grows along every creek
Strap rail is used on railroads in the East too

northerncross.title: Illinois state bonds
northerncross.lead: Lend to the state and collect interest
facts: The State of Illinois promises to pay interest
Bankers in London and Amsterdam are buying
"He can't stop smiling"

northerncross.title: Trouble back East?
facts: New York banks stopped paying out gold and silver in May 1837
Illinois has rich soil and growing towns
The bonds are backed by the state

northerncross.title: Only 3 spots left
northerncross.lead: The state wants its money by the end of the week
facts: "If you wait, the price will go up"
"Guaranteed"
Sign today
